## if / unless / while

`unless` is `if not`. Modifier forms (`return if done`) keep short guards readable. Prefer early returns over deep nesting.

## case / when

`case` uses `===` for matching — so ranges, classes, and regexes work as `when` arms. Great for multi-branch dispatch.

## Looping

`while`/`until` exist, but idiomatic Ruby leans on `each`, `times`, and Enumerable.

blocks.code:
n = 7
label = case n
        when 0 then "zero"
        when 1..9 then "single digit"
        when Integer then "integer"
        else "other"
        end
puts label  # single digit
